correctness.rationale: For finite abelian G and nonempty A, fix g in A and normalize D=A-g, 0 in D, H=<D>. Then A^[j]=jg+jD; jD increases and strictly grows until the first j=s with jD=H, because equality of successive sumsets would force invariance under all of H. This saturation index s is the monogenic semigroup index; eventual period r is order(g+H) in G/H. If s=m>=2, |D|>=2 and successive cardinality increases force |H|>=m+1; quotient needs >=r elements, so |G|>=(m+1)r. For m=1 lower bound r holds. Cyclic host C_((m+1)r) with A={1,1+r} realizes m>=2, and singleton generator in C_r realizes m=1. Equality implies |D|=2, H cyclic generated by difference h of order m+1, G/H cyclic of order r; conversely these suffice. All optimal abelian hosts cyclic precisely when gcd(m+1,r)=1 by primary decomposition; otherwise C_(m+1)×C_r is noncyclic optimal. Independently enumerated all nonempty subsets of cyclic groups n<=9 and 361 cyclic constructions m,r<=19, while the all-order proof rests on monotone sumset stabilization.
